q: A software firm hires a freelancer to design its app, but the written contract never mentions who owns the finished design. What is the safest way to avoid a later ownership dispute?
r: State in the contract who owns the intellectual property
Clear terms prevent later disputes.
w: Wait until the app is finished and then decide
Assume the freelancer keeps ownership by default
That may not match what the firm intended.
Rely on a verbal comment made at the first meeting
Verbal comments are hard to prove.

q: What does an NDA (non-disclosure agreement) protect?
r: Confidential business information from being shared
It limits who may reveal secrets.
w: A product from being sold overseas
An employee's right to a raise

q: A customer signs up for a free trial that turns into a paid subscription without a clear warning. Which concern does this raise?
r: Deceptive or unfair business practices
Hidden terms can violate consumer protection rules.
w: The issue involves customers, not employees.
The issue is not about land use.
The issue is not about trade.

q: Why must a business collect and pay sales tax correctly?
r: It is required by law and noncompliance brings penalties
Tax rules are legally enforced.
w: It increases the store's profit margin
Sales tax belongs to the government.
It is optional for small shops

q: An employee posts false claims on social media that damage a competitor's reputation. Which legal issue could result?
r: Defamation
False statements that harm reputation can lead to lawsuits.
w: That concerns inability to pay debts.

q: What is the main purpose of workplace safety regulations?
r: To protect employees from hazards and injury
Employers must provide a safe environment.
w: To limit how much employees may earn
Safety rules do not set pay limits.
To restrict which customers may shop

q: What does 'bankruptcy' allow a person or business to do?
r: Seek legal relief from debts they cannot pay
Courts oversee the process.
w: Contracts are handled by the process.

q: A landlord refuses to rent to a business owner because of the owner's religion. What is this?
r: Unlawful discrimination
Equal treatment laws prohibit it.
w: Religion is not a lawful basis.

q: What is a contract's consideration?
r: Something of value exchanged by each party
It makes promises binding.
w: A discount offered after a complaint
That is not a required element.
A background check on the signers

q: A manager must tell employees that bonuses will be smaller this year. Which approach is best?
r: Explain the reasons honestly and respectfully, and allow questions
Honesty maintains trust.
w: Announce it by anonymous note and leave
Hide the reason and say nothing

q: What is the purpose of an agenda for a meeting?
r: To list topics and keep the discussion on track
It saves time.
w: To prove the meeting was held

q: A customer service rep must explain a complicated policy to a confused customer. What is the best technique?
r: Use plain language and check for understanding
Clarity helps the customer.
w: Use technical terms to show expertise
Speak faster so the call ends sooner
Read the policy aloud without explanation

q: Which format is most appropriate for a formal job application?
r: A business letter with a résumé
It follows professional conventions.
w: That is not a formal application.

q: Two team members misunderstand each other because one used slang the other did not know. What barrier does this show?
r: A language barrier
Unfamiliar words block understanding.

q: Why is proofreading important before sending a business message?
r: It catches errors that could hurt credibility
Accurate writing looks professional.
w: It removes the need for a clear purpose

q: What is the best way to give constructive criticism?
r: Be specific, respectful and focus on improvement
It helps the person act.
w: Criticize in front of the team

q: A customer says an item arrived broken and wants a refund. The store policy allows exchanges only. What is the best action?
r: Offer the exchange, explain the policy and escalate for a possible exception
The response respects policy and the customer.
w: Say the customer must have broken it
Give a refund without checking policy

q: How can a business show it values customers' time?
r: Reduce waiting and respond promptly
Quick service shows respect.
w: Add more steps to every purchase

q: A call center agent receives a hostile caller. Which response best keeps the call professional?
r: Stay calm, acknowledge the frustration and focus on a solution
Calm responses de-escalate.

q: What does it mean to 'go the extra mile' for a customer?
r: Do more than the customer expects
It creates memorable service.
w: Do only what the policy requires

q: Why should employees know company policies?
r: So they can explain them accurately to customers
Accurate answers reduce confusion.
w: So they can hide them from customers
So they can ignore them when busy
So they can change them freely

q: A company surveys customers and learns that many dislike the long checkout process. What should it do?
r: Study the process and find ways to speed it up
Feedback should drive improvement.
w: Make checkout longer to look careful

q: Which action builds trust with customers?
r: Keeping promises about price, quality and delivery
Reliability builds trust.

q: What is a customer complaint a chance to do?
r: Learn and improve the product or service
Complaints reveal problems.
w: Avoid the customer in the future

q: A drought reduces the supply of wheat. What is the most likely effect on the price of bread?
r: It will tend to rise
Lower supply raises costs and prices.

q: What does a trade deficit mean?
r: Imports exceed exports
A country buys more than it sells abroad.

q: Which situation best shows a negative externality?
r: A factory pollutes a river used by nearby towns
Third parties bear costs they did not choose.
w: A bakery's smell attracts customers who buy bread
A shop sells at a profit

q: What does the unemployment rate measure?
r: The share of the labor force that is jobless and looking for work
It shows labor market conditions.
w: The share of workers who earn the minimum wage
The share of firms that fail each year
The share of people who retire

q: Why might a government use subsidies?
r: To encourage certain activities by lowering costs for producers
Subsidies support chosen goals.
w: To raise prices on all goods

q: What is a free enterprise system?
r: An economy where private owners run businesses for profit
Markets guide most decisions.
w: An economy where the government owns everything

q: A teammate takes credit for your idea in front of the manager. What is the most mature first response?
r: Calmly speak with the teammate privately about it
Direct, respectful talk can resolve it.
w: Embarrass the teammate in a meeting
Refuse to work with anyone again

q: What does being adaptable at work mean?
r: Adjusting to new situations and changes
Flexibility helps teams succeed.

q: How does teamwork benefit a business?
r: Combining skills helps solve problems and reach goals
Collaboration improves results.
w: It removes the need for leaders
It makes work slower in every case

q: A manager is stressed and snaps at an employee. Later, the manager apologizes. What does this show?
r: Accountability and respect for others
Owning behavior repairs trust.
w: Weak leadership that should be hidden
A need to avoid the employee
A way to avoid all feedback

q: What does integrity mean?
r: Doing the right thing even when no one is watching
It means consistent honesty.

q: Which behavior shows respect for coworkers' ideas?
r: Listening without interrupting
Listening shows value.
w: Interrupting to share your own idea

q: A coworker is struggling with a heavy workload. Which response shows empathy and teamwork?
r: Ask what help they need and offer support when possible
It shows care.
w: Report them without speaking to them

q: What is conflict resolution?
r: Finding a fair solution to a disagreement
It helps teams move forward.
w: Winning an argument at any cost

q: A founder cannot afford to hire a full-time employee. Which choice would best control costs while still getting help?
r: Hire a part-time worker or freelancer
Flexible help lowers fixed costs.
w: Do nothing and let work pile up

q: What is a start-up cost?
r: An expense needed to launch a business
Examples include equipment and licenses.
w: A profit from the first sale

q: What does a unique selling proposition (USP) describe?
r: What makes a product different from competitors
It gives customers a reason to choose it.
w: The cost to produce a product

q: A new café owner has few savings and wants to test demand before opening a full shop. What is a smart first step?
r: Run a small pop-up stand or market booth
Testing reduces risk.
w: Sign a long expensive lease immediately
Hire a large staff before selling anything

q: What is a limited liability company (LLC)?
r: A business form that protects owners' personal assets
It combines liability protection with flexibility.
w: A business owned by the government
A business that cannot earn profit

q: Why is record keeping important for a small business?
r: It tracks income and expenses and supports tax filing
Records support decisions.

q: An entrepreneur wins a contract that doubles her workload. Which action best manages growth?
r: Plan resources, staffing and cash flow before accepting more
Planning prevents overload.
w: Promise quick delivery with no plan

q: A store's net income is $12,000 on sales of $120,000. What is its profit margin?
r: $12,000 divided by $120,000 equals 10%.

q: What is a liability?
r: An amount a business owes to others
Loans and accounts payable are liabilities.

q: What is the purpose of savings?
r: To set money aside for future needs or goals
Savings provide security.

q: A person earns $3,000 per month and spends $3,300. What is the likely result?
r: Debt or reduced savings
Spending more than income requires borrowing or draining savings.
w: Spending does not cause a raise.

q: What does APR stand for?
r: Annual percentage rate
It shows the yearly cost of borrowing.

q: Why compare interest rates before choosing a loan?
r: A lower rate reduces the total cost of borrowing
Rates affect total repayment.
w: A higher rate always means better service
Rates have no effect on cost

q: An investor puts all her savings into one company's stock. Which risk is she most exposed to?
r: A lack of diversification
One failure could cause large losses.

q: What is gross pay?
r: Total earnings before deductions
Taxes and benefits are subtracted later.

q: A business has high sales but is always short of cash. Which is a likely cause?
r: Customers pay slowly while bills are due
Timing of cash matters.
w: Sales are too high to record

q: A company wants applicants of many backgrounds. Which recruiting practice would help most?
r: Advertise openings through many channels and communities
Wide outreach reaches more candidates.
w: Post openings in one small place

q: Why do employers conduct background checks?
r: To verify information and reduce hiring risks
Checks support safety and trust.

q: An employee repeatedly arrives late. What is the best first step for a supervisor?
r: Discuss the problem and set clear expectations
Early communication can solve problems.
w: Embarrass the employee in front of the team

q: What does the term 'benefits' mean in compensation?
r: Non-wage rewards such as insurance or paid leave
Benefits add to total pay.

q: A hacker sends an email pretending to be a bank and asks employees to enter passwords. What is this attack called?
r: Phishing
It tricks people into giving information.
w: That protects data by coding it.

q: A manager receives sales data in a long table and wants to spot trends quickly. What should she create?
r: A chart or graph
Visuals show trends clearly.
w: A longer table with more columns

q: What is the purpose of a firewall?
r: To block unauthorized access to a network
It guards against threats.

q: A grocery store notices shoppers buy more when products are displayed at eye level. This is an example of:
r: Using product placement to influence buying
Placement affects choices.

q: What is word-of-mouth marketing?
r: Customers telling others about a business
Personal recommendations build trust.

q: What is a loss leader?
r: A product sold at a low price to attract customers
It draws shoppers to buy other items.
w: A product that cannot be sold
A product that is always free
A product sold only to employees

q: A company runs the same ad on TV, social media and in stores with the same message and look. What is this practice called?
r: Integrated marketing communications
A consistent message across channels strengthens impact.

q: What does a product's life cycle describe?
r: The stages a product goes through from introduction to decline
Marketing changes by stage.
w: The time it takes to manufacture an item
The length of a product warranty
The number of units in stock

q: A restaurant's food waste costs $2,000 per month. Which action best reduces waste?
r: Track what is wasted and adjust orders and portions
Data guides improvement.

q: What is just-in-time (JIT) inventory?
r: Receiving goods only as they are needed
It reduces storage costs.
w: Ordering everything at the start of the year

q: A company wants to cut costs without reducing quality. Which approach is most sensible?
r: Streamline processes to remove waste
Efficiency lowers costs.

q: What is an emergency evacuation plan?
r: Steps for safely leaving a building during danger
Plans save lives.

q: An employee is offered a chance to lead a short project. What is the best reason to accept?
r: It builds leadership skills and shows initiative
It supports career growth.
w: It guarantees a raise next week
It allows avoiding other tasks entirely

q: Which is an example of a long-term career goal?
r: Becoming a department manager within ten years
It is a future target.

q: Why follow the chain of command at work?
r: It keeps communication and decisions organized
Everyone knows who to report to.

q: An applicant is asked 'Tell me about a time you solved a problem.' What is the best way to answer?
r: Describe the situation, your action and the result
A clear example shows skill.
w: Say you have never had a problem

q: What is a professional portfolio?
r: A collection of work samples showing skills
It supports applications.

q: A retailer sees that online sales are growing faster than store sales. Which strategic response is most logical?
r: Invest more in its online presence
Strategy follows trends.
w: That does not respond to the trend.

q: A company is deciding between two expansion plans. What should managers do before choosing?
r: Compare costs, benefits and risks of each plan
Analysis supports a better decision.
w: Choose the first idea without analysis
Wait for a competitor to decide

q: What is delegation?
r: Assigning tasks and authority to others
It lets managers focus on priorities.
